opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted. Requested admin; recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E013: contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; admin is never permitted. Requested admin, so recommending the maximum allowed: read.
reason: The two notes about E013 conflict on employment type: HR note says full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin since Payroll is owned by that role), while the Security record says contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read and never permits admin. Given the conflicting facts, I apply the more restrictive applicable limit. As a contractor with only basic security training, the maximum allowed for Payroll is read, and I never grant more than the requested level (admin). Decision: read.
